written.text: Make a precis of the following passage in about one-third of its original length. Supply a suitable title. (14) The advent of social media has fundamentally altered the landscape of human communication and information exchange. What began as a platform for personal interaction has evolved into a powerful ecosystem that shapes public discourse, influences political processes, drives economic activity, and facilitates the dissemination of knowledge. Social media platforms have transcended geographical boundaries, enabled the rapid circulation of ideas and fostered unprecedented levels of connectivity. In an increasingly digital world, these platforms serve as important channels through which individuals, institutions, and governments engage with diverse audiences in real time. The transformative potential of social media is evident in its capacity to democratize access to information. Educational institutions, libraries, research organizations, and public authorities utilize social media to disseminate knowledge, promote awareness, and encourage civic participation. During emergencies and public health crises, these platforms often function as vital communication tools, enabling the swift transmission of critical information. Furthermore, social media has amplified the voices of marginalized communities, creating opportunities for social advocacy and public engagement that were previously difficult to achieve through traditional media channels. Despite these advantages, the proliferation of social media has generated significant challenges. The speed with which information travels often exceeds the mechanisms available for verification, contributing to the widespread circulation of misinformation and disinformation. The emergence of algorithm-driven content distribution can create echo chambers that reinforce existing beliefs and intensify social polarization. Additionally, concerns regarding data privacy, cybercrime, online harassment, and the commercialization of personal information have raised important ethical and legal questions. The influence of social media on public opinion and electoral processes has further highlighted the need for greater accountability and regulatory oversight. In light of these developments, the effective use of social media requires a balanced approach that maximizes its benefits while mitigating its risks. Digital literacy, critical thinking, and responsible online conduct have become essential competencies for citizens of the twenty-first century. Governments, educational institutions, technology companies, and civil society must collaborate to promote ethical information practices and strengthen mechanisms for content verification. Ultimately, social media is neither inherently beneficial nor harmful; its impact depends on how individuals and societies choose to employ this powerful technological instrument. When guided by responsibility, transparency, and informed participation, social media can serve as a catalyst for knowledge dissemination, democratic engagement, and social progress.

Write a letter to the Secretary, Law & Judicial Department, emphasizing the need for establishing a Statewide Digital Legal Information Network connecting court libraries, law college libraries, and public legal information centres. Discuss its benefits for legal research, judicial efficiency, and public access to justice.(10)

Read the following passage carefully and answer the questions that follow. The emergence of the knowledge economy has transformed the foundations of economic growth and social development. Unlike traditional economies that relied primarily on physical resources and manual labour, modern economies increasingly depend on the creation, dissemination, and application of knowledge. Information, innovation, and intellectual capital have become critical assets in determining productivity and competitiveness. In this context, libraries have evolved into important institutions that facilitate access to knowledge and support the development of an informed and skilled society. A defining feature of the knowledge economy is the importance of information accessibility. Access to reliable and timely information enables individuals to make informed decisions, acquire new skills, and participate effectively in economic and social activities. However, inequalities in access to information can widen existing social and economic disparities. Libraries help address this challenge by providing equitable access to authoritative sources of knowledge. Through their collections, digital resources, and community services, they promote educational opportunities and contribute to social inclusion. The rapid advancement of digital technology has significantly expanded the role of libraries. Digital repositories, electronic databases, and online information services have extended library services beyond physical locations. At the same time, the abundance of information available through digital platforms has increased the risk of misinformation and information overload. Consequently, libraries have assumed a vital role in promoting information literacy. Librarians now guide users in identifying credible sources, evaluating information critically, and using information ethically and responsibly. Libraries also constitute an essential component of a nation’s knowledge infrastructure. By supporting research, innovation, and lifelong learning, they contribute to intellectual development and economic progress. Academic, legal, scientific, and public libraries provide access to specialized resources that facilitate scholarly inquiry and evidence-based decision-making. Despite challenges such as financial constraints, technological change, and evolving user expectations, libraries continue to adapt and remain relevant. As societies become increasingly knowledge-driven, libraries serve not only as repositories of information but also as dynamic institutions that empower individuals, strengthen communities, and promote sustainable development. subparts.a: What is meant by the term “knowledge economy”?(2)
subparts.b: How do libraries help reduce social and economic inequalities?(2)
subparts.c: Why is information literacy important in the digital age?(2)
subparts.d: How has digital technology simultaneously enhanced and complicated the role of libraries?(2) (2)
